prompt: A researcher fits a least-squares line to data from $20$ randomly chosen farms, relating fertilizer amount to corn yield. For the $t$-test of the slope, $H_0: \beta = 0$, how many degrees of freedom are used?
hint: A regression line is described by two estimated numbers. Each estimated parameter costs one degree of freedom.

hints.text: A regression line is described by two estimated numbers. Each estimated parameter costs one degree of freedom.
The slope and the intercept are both estimated, so the rule is df $= n - 2$. Here $n = 20$ farms.
$20 - 2 = 18$, so the test uses $18$ degrees of freedom.

explanation: For inference about a regression slope, the $t$ distribution has $n - 2$ degrees of freedom.
Two are lost because both the intercept and the slope are estimated from the data.
With $20$ farms, the degrees of freedom are $20 - 2 = 18$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare with a one-sample t
steps: A one-sample $t$-test estimates one thing (the mean), so df $= n - 1$.
A regression line estimates two things, so it loses two: df $= n - 2$.
